poster_title: A Comprehensive Survey of Reward Models: Taxonomy, Applications, Challenges, and Future Directions
authors: Jialun Zhong, Wei Shen, Yanzeng Li, Songyang Gao, Hua Lu, Yicheng Chen, Yang Zhang, Wei Zhou, Jinjie Gu, Lei Zou
paper_info: 2023, Comprehensive introduction to Reward Models in the LLM era

panels.headline: First comprehensive survey focused on RMs in the LLM era
content: Large Language Models (LLMs) have seen rapid development, enhancing AI capabilities and driving advances in various downstream tasks.
Alignment techniques are crucial for ensuring LLMs adhere to human values, and Reward Models (RMs) trained on human preference data can serve as proxies for human preferences.
RMs are essential for aligning LLMs with human values and have shown significant potential in various applications.
Future research should focus on improving the efficiency and quality of preference collection, enhancing reward modeling techniques, and exploring AI preferences.
High costs associated with human annotators for preference collection.

panels.headline: RMs trained on human preference data can serve as proxies for human preferences
content: LLMs have enhanced AI capabilities and driven advances in various downstream tasks.
Alignment techniques are crucial for ensuring LLMs adhere to human values.
Human preferences are essential but costly and challenging to collect.
RMs can provide reward signals for reinforcement learning, guiding LLMs' behavior.
Combining AI and human preferences can enhance the quality and efficiency of RM training.

panels.headline: Taxonomy of Reward Models, including Preference Collections, Reward Modeling, and Usage
content: RMs can be trained on human preference data to provide reward signals for reinforcement learning.
Active learning techniques improve the efficiency of preference collection.

panels.headline: Various methods for human preference collection, including active learning, data augmentation, and sequential pairwise comparison
content: Various methods for human preference collection are explored, including active learning, data augmentation, and sequential pairwise comparison.
Different types of RMs, such as discriminative, generative, and implicit reward models, are compared.

panels.headline: Generative RMs show promise in providing more nuanced and context-aware reward signals
content: RMs trained on human preference data can effectively guide LLMs' behavior in alignment tasks.
Generative RMs provide more nuanced and context-aware reward signals.
